texts.facts: The respondents have filed an application for vacating the stay mainly on the ground that the petitioner is having remedy of appeal under Section 46(4) of the Food Safety & Standards Act, 2006 hence, stay be vacated and petition be dismissed. Shri Shrivastava has produced copy of the order dated 01.02.2016 passed by the coordinate bench of this Court in W.P.No.2665/2013, by which the similar application for vacating stay has been rejected filed on the ground that alternate efficacious remedy is available. "I.A.No.309/16, an application for dismissal of the petition filed by the State primarily raises three grounds. The first being that the petitioner can approach the Food Safely Appellate Tribunal under Section 70 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 (in short the Act, 2006) against the order of Adjudicating Officer under Section 68 of the Act. Even otherwise, this petition is pending since 2014 and interim order is still in operation.
texts.arguments: Further, it is contended that vide Annexure-A/2 (alongwith I.A.No.309/16), the coordinate bench at principal seat in W.P.No.19958/13 has relegated the petitioner therein to avail the remedy of appeal and lastly by relying on Annexure-A/3, it is contended that similar petitions have been dismissed by the single bench at the principal seat. The present petition assails the prosecution launched against the petitioner and also sanction granted for prosecuting the petitioner under the said Act, 2006 on various grounds. In the instant case, the petitioner's product, i.e. cream biscuits have been found to be misbranded. Learned senior counsel for the petitioner fairly submits that petitioners are also interested in early disposal of this petition as number of petitions are pending before all the three benches of this Court.
